To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction of electromagnetic radiation in a wide frequency range with arrays consisting of carbon nanotube matrix and ferromagnetic nanoparticles leads to the emergence and disappearance of resonances, namely, the emergence of peaks and valleys in frequency dependences of the permeability, reflection and transmission coefficients.

the magnetic nanoparticles in carbon nanotubes are capable of resonant absorption and scattering of electromagnetic radiation in a broad frequency range from 20 to 200 GHz, and this is due to the interaction of electromagnetic radiation in these frequency ranges with the resonance resistive–capacitive–inductive circuits formed by the magnetic nanoparticles and the interface between the nanoparticles and the carbon nanotubes.

the interaction of electromagnetic radiation in a frequency range of 20–200 GHz with a carbon nanotube matrix filled with ferromagnetic particles can lead to the formation of resonances, which are manifested in the form of peaks and valleys in frequency dependencies of the permeability, and in the reflection and transmission coefficients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using the proposed model to design a magnetic nanocomposites with a tunable magnetic response to electromagnetic radiation.
the possibility of creating new materials for microwave engineering based on magnetic carbon nanotube composites.

the interaction of electromagnetic radiation in a wide frequency range with a magnetic nanomaterial based on carbon nanomaterials with embedded ferromagnetic nanoparticles, and the influence of the morphology of the nanocomposites on the interaction of electromagnetic waves with the nanomaterial.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic nanocomposite is a promising material for the creation of new devices for microwave and millimeter wave technology.

the interaction of electromagnetic radiation in a broad frequency range (20–200 GHz) with arrays of CNT with ferromagnetic inclusions is characterized by a complex dependence of the reflection coefficient and transmission coefficient on the frequency.
the presence of ferromagnetic nanoparticles in the carbon nanotube matrix can significantly affect the properties of the material in a broad frequency range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed approach can be used to create nanocomposites with a controlled frequency response in the microwave frequency range.

the proposed model allows us to predict the behavior of the electromagnetic properties of magnetic nanocomposites with a CNT matrix, and to explain the experimental results of the frequency dependence of reflection and transmission of nanocomposites with different types of nanoparticles.

the interaction of electromagnetic radiation in a wide frequency range with magnetic nanocomposites based on carbon nanofilms is a promising area of study, which can find practical application in the development of nanocomposite materials with a wide range of applications in the field of electromagnetic compatibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of ferromagnetic nanoparticles on the surface of carbon nanotube arrays allows for the creation of nanocomposite materials with a wide range of permeability values, which can be used in microwave absorbers.
the presence of ferromagnetic nanoparticles in the CNT matrix leads to a change in the frequency dependence, and therefore the absorption, of electromagnetic radiation in a broad frequency range.

the interaction of electromagnetic radiation in this frequency range with the magnetic nanocomposite is characterized by a strong dependence on the concentration and size of the ferromagnetic nanoparticles and on the length and diameter of CNT.
